posts.reason: A full style reference that gives the reasoning and exceptions for every rule, from trait design to error handling, and a technical thread on the non_exhaustive rule where people with large codebases argue forward-compatible enums against exhaustive matches.

A concrete description of layered review when an agent writes most of the code, with risk-tiered human approvals, merge queues, flags and REVIEW.md files, and a skeptical thread that asks whether any of it fits a small team.

Short illustrated sections, each with a code sample and its current browser support, and a large thread that turns into an argument over whether plain HTML, CSS and JS can handle state without a framework.

A long benchmark with full method, per-image quality charts and decode time and memory tables, ending in a clear default for the web, and a thread that flags which lossless numbers cannot yet be checked.

A programmer expecting his first child works through what education is for, leaning on Neil Postman and Edison's old predictions about schools, and a 600-comment thread of parents arguing over what is still worth teaching.
Practitioners share how they keep shipped code understandable, by designing abstractions first, sketching in pseudo-code and reviewing before every commit.
Company telemetry, a comparison of adopting and non-adopting engineers, surveys and interviews, read alongside a thread that doubts commit counts measure anything.
A short interactive build-up from tiny parsers to a working one, and a thread that compares the idea across Haskell, Rust and Python.

One experiment, with traffic and citation counts, tracing invented statistics as a chatbot kept fetching them after the search engine dropped the site and other pages repeated them, and a thread that asks whether fetching proves use and whether regulation can help.
A dated, sourced history of how bolt-on iron fire escapes became the default and were later replaced, and how building codes lock in early choices.
